To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
bacterial chromosomes have defined spatial arrangements that preserve the linear order of the genetic map.
the bacterial chromosome is organized as large macrodomains that are reorganized at specific steps of cell cycle.

the chromosome of E. coli has a ring organization that consists of four macrodomains, two of which are structured and two are less so, and that these macrodomains are defined in a cell cycle‐dependent manner by the spatial distribution of DNA sites.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the spatial arrangement of bacterial chromosomes, with the identification of large regions defined as'macrodomains' and with their possible organization.
the spatial organization and dynamics of bacterial chromosomes during the cell cycle, and the development of methods to analyze these properties in vivo.
the spatial organization of the chromosome of the bacterial model organism Escherichia coli.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

bacterial chromosomes are organized in large macrodomains with a defined spatial arrangement and that the Ori and Ter regions have specific functions in chromosome organization and segregation during the cell cycle.

the bacterial chromosome is organized in macrodomains that relocalize at different steps of the cell division cycle, and that the macrodomain organization is a conserved property of the bacterial chromosome, although the precise nature of the macrodomain organization may vary between species.
the chromosome of E. coli has a ring organization.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the chromosome of E. coli has a ring organization.

the bacterial chromosome is organized as macrodomains, which are large regions with a specific spatial arrangement that are relocalized during the cell cycle to specific positions within the cell, and that these macrodomains have a ring organization with two less‐structured macrodomains flanking four structured macrodomains.
the E. coli chromosome is organized in a ring‐like structure with four macrodomains and that this organization is essential for its proper replication.
The main takeaway from our work is that
bacteria have a defined spatial organization of the chromosome that preserves the linear gene order.
bacteria have a chromosome organization that is not random.
bacterial chromosomes are highly organized and have a ring structure with four macrodomains that are organized in a specific order.
